card.name: Kipas Pakarena
card.era: Heritage of the Gowa Kingdom (16th-18th century)
card.tagline: Graceful Makassar fan dance of the Gowa court
card.profile: Kipas Pakarena is a fan dance originating from Gowa, South Sulawesi, a cultural tradition of the Makassar people dating to the Gowa Kingdom (id.Wikipedia; Indonesia-Tourism). The name combines 'pa' (the performer) and 'karena' (to play). Performed by women holding folding fans with slow, gentle movements, it depicts the farewell of the Boting Langi (heaven dwellers) and Lino (earth dwellers), with movements expressing the gentleness, loyalty, modesty and respect of Gowa women. Dancers wear the silk Baju Bodo and lipa' sa'be sarong, accompanied by seven male musicians playing the gandrang drum and puik-puik. A full performance can last nearly two hours.
card.insight: Dancers are bound by strict rules - they may not open their eyes wide or raise their feet high - demanding great stamina to sustain the dance's restrained grace across its roughly two-hour, twelve-part structure (Indonesia-Tourism; Kompas).
card.image_significance: Royal fan dance of the Gowa sultanate. A representative image shows gilded costume, angular hand poses and a temple or court setting — Gowa (Makassar), Indonesia.
